method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading; exact macro, identifier, token and formula comparison; and replay of the isomorphism, induction and successor-characterization arguments. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Standard models of arithmetic: definition, standard-numeral domain characterization, the Q-based converse, uniqueness of the standard isomorphism and the successor-function characterization on a countably infinite carrier.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every element of a standard model is the value of a standard numeral because an isomorphism from N is surjective. Such names select the elements without asserting that the carrier objects literally are natural numbers, and the converse domain condition alone can fail.
samples.checks: The inclusion and surjectivity directions, existential numeral index, warning about carrier identity and converse problem are all preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A model of Q whose domain is exhausted by numeral values is standard. The numeral-value map is surjective by hypothesis, injective because Q distinguishes unequal numerals, and preserves zero, successor, addition, multiplication and strict order.
samples.checks: The proof retains both directions of the order relation, the non-satisfaction case when n is not below m and every displayed preservation equation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The numeral-value isomorphism is the only isomorphism from N to a standard model: any other isomorphism agrees at zero and then at every successor by induction.
samples.checks: The base case, induction hypothesis and seven-line successor calculation keep the same direction and hypotheses.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Any countably infinite carrier can support a standard model after choosing zero and a successor bijection from the carrier onto the carrier without zero; the other operations and order are then fixed. Successor omits zero, is injective and reaches every nonzero element.
samples.checks: The two displayed first-order sentences keep their intended constraints. The source's mistaken reference to an element outside the domain is repaired to outside the range, which is the exact failure of surjectivity.

source_observations: The standard-model and standard-numeral terminology follows T281 and T282, while the source equations control the carrier-independent isomorphism sense.
The proof from Q uses numeral inequality for injectivity and separately verifies every constant, function and relation component needed for an isomorphism.
The frozen source's final surjectivity explanation says domain where its displayed function type and the following predecessor sentence require range; OLFOL-030 records the bounded prose correction.
All macros, identifiers, controlled tokens and formulas match the frozen source exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact full Marathi standard-model terminology remains expert-reviewable.
